title: Lost in Moderation: How Commercial Content Moderation APIs Over- and Under-Moderate Group-Targeted Hate Speech and Linguistic Variations
base_benchmarks: Identity Phrase Templates from Dixon et al. [23]
findings: All tested APIs tend to over-moderate content related to Jewish and Muslim people. They heavily rely on group identity tokens (e.g., 'Jew', 'Islam', 'Muslim', 'christians') to classify hate speech, leading to misclassification of neutral, descriptive, or reclaimed speech. This bias is entrenched, with spurious correlations (e.g., 'israeli' for Jewish identity) exacerbating over-moderation. Google's API, in particular, showed a high false positive rate for content mentioning Jewish and Muslim groups.
